claim: Mechanical load on the αβ T-cell receptor (TCR) is crucial for recognizing the antigenic peptide-bound major histocompatibility complex (pMHC) molecule.
source: Increasing evidence suggests that mechanical load on the αβ T-cell receptor (TCR) is crucial for recognizing the antigenic peptide-bound major histocompatibility complex (pMHC) molecule.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to existing literature as indicated by the phrase 'Increasing evidence suggests'.

claim: All-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that the inter-domain motion of the TCR is responsible for the load-induced catch bond behavior of the TCR-pMHC complex and peptide discrimination.
source: Our recent all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that the inter-domain motion of the TCR is responsible for the load-induced catch bond behavior of the TCR-pMHC complex and peptide discrimination (Chang-Gonzalez et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study (Chang-Gonzalez et al., 2024).

claim: The B7 TCR-pMHC interface stabilizes under ∼15 pN load using a conserved dynamic allostery mechanism that involves the asymmetric motion of the TCR chassis.
source: We find that the B7 TCR-pMHC interface stabilizes under ∼15 pN load using a conserved dynamic allostery mechanism that involves the asymmetric motion of the TCR chassis.
evidence: The claim is supported by the MD simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: B7 has fewer high-occupancy contacts with pMHC compared to A6 despite forming comparable contacts in the crystal structure.
source: However, despite forming comparable contacts with pMHC as A6 in the crystal structure, B7 has fewer high-occupancy contacts with pMHC and exhibits higher mechanical compliance during the simulation.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of simulation data between B7 and A6 TCRs.

claim: B7 exhibits higher mechanical compliance during the simulation compared to A6.
source: However, despite forming comparable contacts with pMHC as A6 in the crystal structure, B7 has fewer high-occupancy contacts with pMHC and exhibits higher mechanical compliance during the simulation.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data comparing B7 and A6 TCRs.

claim: The dynamic allostery common to the TCRαβ chassis can amplify slight differences in interfacial contacts into distinctive mechanical responses and nuanced biological outcomes.
source: These results indicate that the dynamic allostery common to the TCRαβ chassis can amplify slight differences in interfacial contacts into distinctive mechanical responses and nuanced biological outcomes.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the simulation results comparing A6 and B7 TCRs.

claim: A6 and B7 TCRs are both specific for the same Tax peptide (LLFGYPVYV) of the human T lymphotropic virus 1 (HTLV-1) bound to HLA-A2.
source: The A6 T-cell receptor (TCR)αβ and B7 TCRαβ (herein we call TCRαβ simply as TCR) are both specific for the same Tax peptide (LLFGYPVYV) of the human T lymphotropic virus 1 (HTLV-1) bound to HLA-A2 (Garboczi et al., 1996a, Garboczi et al., 1996b; Ding et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: A6 and B7 derive from T-cell clones isolated from two patients with HTLV-1-associated myelopathic/tropical spastic paraparesis.
source: A6 and B7 derive from T-cell clones isolated from two patients with HTLV-1-associated myelopathic/tropical spastic paraparesis (Utz et al., 1996; Ding et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A6 and B7 share the same Vβ germline gene (TRBV6-5) and differ only in the Vα germline gene (A6: TRAV12-2; B7:TRAV29/DV5).
source: They share the same Vβ germline gene (TRBV6-5) and differ only in the Vα germline gene (A6: TRAV12-2; B7:TRAV29/DV5), with sequence similarity of 45% for Vα, 96% for Vβ, and 100% for Cα and Cβ (Ding et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The sequence similarity between A6 and B7 is 45% for Vα, 96% for Vβ, and 100% for Cα and Cβ.
source: They share the same Vβ germline gene (TRBV6-5) and differ only in the Vα germline gene (A6: TRAV12-2; B7:TRAV29/DV5), with sequence similarity of 45% for Vα, 96% for Vβ, and 100% for Cα and Cβ (Ding et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The only structural differences between A6 and B7 TCRs are from the residues of the Vα domain and the highly variable complementarity-determining region 3 (CDR3β) loop of the Vβ domain.
source: The only structural differences between the two TCRs are from the residues of the Vα domain and the highly variable complementarity-determining region 3 (CDR3β) loop of the Vβ domain that is crucial for peptide recognition (Ding et al., 1998; Bourcier et al., 2001; Rudolph et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: The CDR3β loop of the Vβ domain is crucial for peptide recognition.
source: The only structural differences between the two TCRs are from the residues of the Vα domain and the highly variable complementarity-determining region 3 (CDR3β) loop of the Vβ domain that is crucial for peptide recognition (Ding et al., 1998; Bourcier et al., 2001; Rudolph et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Both A6 and B7 TCRs bind in a diagonal orientation to the Tax peptide-bound MHC in crystal structures.
source: In crystal structures, both TCRs bind in a diagonal orientation to the Tax peptide-bound major histocompatibility complex (pMHC), such that both Vα and Vβ contact the MHC α1 and α2 helices (Garboczi et al., 1996a).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous structural study.

claim: Both Vα and Vβ contact the MHC α1 and α2 helices in the A6 and B7 TCR-pMHC crystal structures.
source: In crystal structures, both TCRs bind in a diagonal orientation to the Tax peptide-bound major histocompatibility complex (pMHC), such that both Vα and Vβ contact the MHC α1 and α2 helices (Garboczi et al., 1996a).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous structural study.

claim: The similar diagonal binding modes of A6 and B7 are achieved by interactions involving different CDR residues contacting largely the same sets of pMHC residues.
source: The similar diagonal binding modes are achieved by interactions involving different CDR residues of A6 and B7 contacting largely the same sets of pMHC residues (Ding et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous structural study.

claim: Only 1 out of 17 residues contacting pMHC in B7 is also found in the A6 pMHC interaction.
source: Only 1 out of 17 residues contacting pMHC in B7 is also found in the A6 pMHC interaction (Ding et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous structural study.

claim: Single-residue mutations to the Tax peptide elicit different responses in A6 and B7 TCRs.
source: T-cell response assays demonstrated that single-residue mutations to the Tax peptide elicit different responses in the two TCRs (Ding et al., 1998; Hausmann et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: The pocket for the Tax peptide Y5 residue is positively charged in A6 but negatively charged in B7.
source: Interfacial interactions may play a role in this TCR-specific response, as residue charges at the surface of the A6 and B7 variable domains show different electrostatic profiles, where the pocket for the Tax peptide Y5 residue is positively charged in A6 but negatively charged in B7 (Ding et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous structural study.

claim: The B7 Vα surface has fewer charged residues exposed than A6 Vα.
source: Overall, the B7 Vα surface has fewer charged residues exposed than A6 Vα.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of structural features between A6 and B7.

claim: A6 and B7 recognize Tax-MHC with similar affinities and kinetics.
source: While A6 and B7 recognize Tax-MHC with similar affinities and kinetics, it has been suggested that they achieve binding via different thermodynamic pathways (Davis-Harrison et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: A6 and B7 achieve binding via different thermodynamic pathways.
source: While A6 and B7 recognize Tax-MHC with similar affinities and kinetics, it has been suggested that they achieve binding via different thermodynamic pathways (Davis-Harrison et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study and involves speculation about binding mechanisms.

claim: The TCR-pMHC bond lifetime under physiological piconewton (pN) level load is more functionally relevant than the equilibrium binding pathway.
source: However, since αβTCR is a mechanosensor (Reinherz et al., 2023), the TCR-pMHC bond lifetime under physiological piconewton (pN) level load should be more functionally relevant than the equilibrium binding pathway.
evidence: The claim is based on citation to previous work and inference about functional relevance.

claim: Contacts with pMHC of A6 and JM22 TCRs are stabilized when an adequate 15–20 pN force is applied.
source: In this regard, we have previously used all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to show that contacts with pMHC of A6 (Chang-Gonzalez et al., 2024) and JM22 (Hwang et al., 2020) TCRs are stabilized when an adequate 15–20 pN force is applied.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous simulation studies.

claim: Force-induced stabilization occurs as the asymmetric domain motion of the TCR chassis leads to weakening of the interface with pMHC either in the absence of an adequate level of force or if the sequence of the bound peptide is incompatible with maintaining contacts in the loaded state.
source: The force-induced stabilization occurs as the asymmetric domain motion of the TCR chassis leads to weakening of the interface with pMHC either in the absence of an adequate level of force or if the sequence of the bound peptide is incompatible with maintaining contacts in the loaded state.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from previous simulation results.

claim: The mechanism of dynamic allostery is largely conserved in B7.
source: We find that the mechanism of dynamic allostery is largely conserved in B7, yet the loaded state does not stabilize contacts with pMHC as robustly as in the A6.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data comparing B7 with A6.

claim: The loaded state does not stabilize contacts with pMHC in B7 as robustly as in A6.
source: We find that the mechanism of dynamic allostery is largely conserved in B7, yet the loaded state does not stabilize contacts with pMHC as robustly as in the A6.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data comparing B7 with A6.

claim: A6 appears to exhibit a stronger catch bond behavior under load compared to B7.
source: Thus, while both A6 and B7 possess comparable equilibrium binding affinity for pMHC, A6 appears to exhibit a stronger catch bond behavior under load.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation data comparing A6 and B7.

claim: Difference in mechanical response between A6 and B7 suggests T-cell clones bearing those TCRs may operate differently in vivo.
source: Given the nuanced and dynamic nature of TCRs against the same pMHC, including the effect of ligand abundance (Akitsu et al., 2024), difference in mechanical response between A6 and B7 suggests T-cell clones bearing those TCRs may operate differently in vivo.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation results and citation to previous work on ligand abundance effects.

claim: The number of high-occupancy contacts were more numerous for B7high compared to B70 and B7low, indicative of a catch bond behavior.
source: Compared to the no- (B70) and low-load (B7low) cases, the number of high-occupancy contacts were more numerous for the high-load case (B7high), indicative of a catch bond behavior.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Absence of the C-module (Vαβ-pMHC) promoted more contacts with pMHC, suggesting the allosteric role of the C-module for binding with pMHC.
source: Absence of the C-module (Vαβ-pMHC) also promoted more contacts with pMHC, suggesting the allosteric role of the C-module for binding with pMHC (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1C and involves inference about the role of the C-module.

claim: The number of pMHC contacts with B7 was reduced compared to A6.
source: However, the number of pMHC contacts with B7 was reduced compared to A6 (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of simulation data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: B7high had overall more inter- and intramolecular contacts than B7low, suggesting that the increased load stiffens the TCR-pMHC complex.
source: B7high had overall more inter- and intramolecular contacts (more orange-yellow circles) than B7low (more purple), suggesting that the increased load stiffens the TCR-pMHC complex.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1D and involves inference about the effect of load.

claim: B70 had fewer TCR-pMHC contacts but more intra-TCR contacts, indicating decoupling of the TCR from pMHC in the absence of load.
source: B70 had fewer TCR-pMHC contacts but more intra-TCR contacts (horizontal bars in Figure 1D), indicating decoupling of the TCR from pMHC in the absence of load.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1D and involves inference about the effect of load absence.

claim: After about 1300 ns, B7high started to lose the initial high-occupancy contacts.
source: However, after about 1300 ns, B7high started to lose the initial high-occupancy contacts (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The fixed extension imposed in simulation can adversely impact the interfacial stability of the B7 TCR-pMHC complex that has a higher compliance than A6.
source: This is likely because the fixed extension (end-to-end distance) imposed in simulation can adversely impact the interfacial stability of the B7 TCR-pMHC complex that has a higher compliance than A6, as discussed further below.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation results.

claim: Interfacial contacts were dominated by MHC-Vα for both A6 and B7 TCRs.
source: Comparing average counts of high-occupancy pMHC contacts for both A6 and B7 TCRs indicates that interfacial contacts were dominated by MHC-Vα (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Vα formed more contacts with MHC than Vβ, while Vβ formed more contacts with the peptide than it does with MHC.
source: Also, Vα formed more contacts with MHC than Vβ, while Vβ formed more contacts with the peptide than it does with MHC (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: B7high and Vαβ-pMHC exhibit more persistent contact profiles compared to B70 and B7low.
source: Similar to A6 (Chang-Gonzalez et al., 2024), occupancy heat maps for individual contact residue pairs show reduced or fragmented contacts for B70 and B7low (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B, more red compared to blue) while B7high and Vαβ-pMHC exhibit more persistent contact profiles (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D, more blue compared to red).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The breakage of high-occupancy contacts in B7high is not due to a high force, but instead happened when instantaneous force was low.
source: Importantly, the breakage is not due to a high force, but instead it happened when instantaneous force was low.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of simulation data relating force and contact stability.

claim: The difference in extension between B7low and B7high is 16.3 Å whereas it is 5.1 Å for A6, for similar ∼5 pN difference between low- and high-load cases.
source: The difference in extension between B7low and B7high is 16.3 Å whereas it is 5.1 Å for A6 (Table 1), for similar ∼5 pN difference between low- and high-load cases.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Table 1.

claim: Being more compliant, the interface of B7 can reach a low-force state more easily, hence it is more prone to destabilization.
source: Being more compliant, the interface of B7 can reach a low-force state more easily, hence it is more prone to destabilization.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation data about B7's mechanical properties.

claim: Location of V-module residues forming contacts with pMHC with greater than 50% average occupancy were concentrated along the peptide for B7high and Vαβ-pMHC, but scattered in B70 and B7low.
source: Location of V-module residues forming contacts with pMHC with greater than 50% average occupancy were concentrated along the peptide for B7high and Vαβ-pMHC, but scattered in B70 and B7low (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Concentration of high-occupancy contacts may protect TCR-pMHC interactions from breakage by water.
source: Such concentration of high-occupancy contacts may protect TCR-pMHC interactions from breakage by water.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation observations.

claim: In A6 and JM22 TCRs, the greater number of contacts with pMHC in the high-load cases and Vαβ-pMHC correlated with larger buried surface area (BSA) of the residues forming contacts.
source: In A6 and JM22 TCRs, the greater number of contacts with pMHC in the high-load cases and Vαβ-pMHC correlated with larger buried surface area (BSA) of the residues forming contacts (Chang-Gonzalez et al., 2024; Hwang et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous simulation studies.

claim: B7 did not follow the trend of greater contacts correlating with larger BSA, as B7high and Vαβ-pMHC had reduced total and per-residue BSA than B70 and B7low.
source: B7 did not follow this trend, as B7high and Vαβ-pMHC had reduced total and per-residue BSA than B70 and B7low (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The fewer high-occupancy contacts in B7 tend to be more exposed, making the relationship between the BSA and load less direct.
source: This is likely because the fewer high-occupancy contacts in B7 (Figure 1C) tend to be more exposed, making the relationship between the BSA and load less direct.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation data.

claim: The total BSA of B7 was 67.4% (B70) to 44.2% (B7high) of the corresponding values of A6.
source: Consistent with this, the total BSA of B7 was 67.4% (B70) to 44.2% (B7high) of the corresponding values of A6.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of simulation data between B7 and A6.

claim: The residues of pMHC forming greater than 50% average occupancy under high load differed between A6 and B7.
source: The residues of pMHC forming greater than 50% average occupancy under high load differed between A6 and B7 (Figure 2E), as did the location of V-module residues forming respective contacts with the pMHC residues (Figure 2C), further highlighting their divergence in the interfacial footprint under load.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figures 2C and 2E.

claim: The root mean square fluctuation (RMSF) of Cα atoms of the Tax peptide measured after 500 ns was reduced in B7high and Vαβ-pMHC compared to B70 and B7low.
source: Despite this, the root mean square fluctuation (RMSF) of Cα atoms of the Tax peptide measured after 500 ns was reduced in B7high and Vαβ-pMHC compared to B70 and B7low (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E), as observed for A6 (Chang-Gonzalez et al., 2024), which supports load-induced stabilization of the complex.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The distance between the V-module and pMHC was stably maintained in Vαβ-pMHC and B7high whereas it fluctuated more in B70 and B7low.
source: The distance was stably maintained in Vαβ-pMHC and B7high (before 1300 ns) whereas it fluctuated more in B70 and B7low.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Vαβ-pMHC and B7high maintained the distance between V-module and pMHC greater than that in the crystal structure by 0.3–0.9 Å.
source: Of note, the former two systems maintained the distance greater than that in the crystal structure by 0.3–0.9 Å.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of simulation data with crystal structure.

claim: A slight separation engendered by force or in the absence of constraint imposed by the C-module provides room for adjusting residues to form more stable contacts.
source: Thus, a slight separation engendered by force or in the absence of constraint imposed by the C-module provides room for adjusting residues to form more stable contacts.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation observations.

claim: The greater number of Vα-Vβ contacts in B70 is consistent with the increase in total intra-TCR contact occupancy.
source: The greater number of Vα-Vβ contacts in B70 (Figure 3A) is consistent with the increase in total intra-TCR contact occupancy (horizontal bar in Figure 1D, bottom panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figures 3A and 1D.

claim: Without load, the greater number of Vα-Vβ contacts does not translate to a stronger TCR-pMHC interface.
source: Without load this does not translate to a stronger TCR-pMHC interface explained above.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation results.

claim: B7 in general had fewer Vα-Vβ contacts (11.0–16.3) than A6 (15.9–23.1).
source: B7 in general had fewer Vα-Vβ contacts (11.0–16.3) than A6 (15.9–23.1) (Chang-Gonzalez et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of simulation data with previous study.

claim: The ∼70% reduction in Vα-Vβ contacts for B7 is comparable to the ∼50% reduction in contacts with pMHC between the two TCRs.
source: The ∼70% reduction in Vα-Vβ contacts for B7 is comparable to the ∼50% reduction in contacts with pMHC between the two TCRs (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of simulation data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: PC amplitude was the lowest for B7high and Vαβ-pMHC, which is consistent with the greater number of Vα-Vβ contacts.
source: PC amplitude was the lowest for B7high and Vαβ-pMHC (Figure 3C), which is consistent with the greater number of Vα-Vβ contacts.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 3C and involves inference about the relationship between PC amplitude and contacts.

claim: CDR3 distance is the shortest for B7high followed by Vαβ-pMHC.
source: Measuring the distance between CDR3α and CDR3β ('CDR3 distance') revealed that this distance is the shortest for B7high followed by Vαβ-pMHC.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data analysis.

claim: The CDR3 distance of the B7 crystal structure is 12.0 Å, which is larger than those of B7high and Vαβ-pMHC.
source: In comparison, the CDR3 distance of the B7 crystal structure is 12.0 Å, which is larger than those of B7high and Vαβ-pMHC (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of simulation data with crystal structure shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The slight separation between the V-module and pMHC in Vαβ-pMHC and B7high allows CDR3 loops to come closer together compared to the crystal structure, akin to pinching the central protrusion of the peptide.
source: The slight separation between the V-module and pMHC (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F) in Vαβ-pMHC and B7high allows CDR3 loops to come closer together compared to the crystal structure, akin to pinching the central protrusion of the peptide.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The number of high-occupancy contacts for the Cα-Cβ interface (26.2–27.5) was considerably greater than those for Vα-Vβ (11.2–16.3), indicating that the C-module acts as a single base for the V-C motion.
source: The number of high-occupancy contacts for the Cα-Cβ interface (26.2–27.5) was considerably greater than those for Vα-Vβ (11.2–16.3), indicating that the C-module acts as a single base for the V-C motion, as noted for A6 and JM22 TCRs (Hwang et al., 2020; Chang-Gonzalez et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data and involves inference about the role of the C-module.

claim: There were fewer high-occupancy contacts for the Vα-Cα interface compared to the Vβ-Cβ interface.
source: Continuing this general feature, there were fewer high-occupancy contacts for the Vα-Cα interface compared to the Vβ-Cβ interface (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: PC1 corresponding to the V-C bending in B7high was similar in other systems, whereas B7low differed the most.
source: PC motion directions were compared by calculating the dot products between the corresponding PC vectors (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A). PC1 corresponding to the V-C bending in B7high (Figure 4B) was similar in other systems, whereas B7low differed the most (darker color for B7low in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, PC1).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Amplitudes of PC1 show a clear distinction where the unliganded Tαβ and B7low were more mobile than B70 and B7high.
source: Amplitudes of PC1 show a clear distinction where the unliganded Tαβ and B7low were more mobile than B70 and B7high (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Vα moves more relative to the C-module than Vβ.
source: Comparing PC amplitudes of the elements of the BOC between α and β chains revealed that Vα moves more relative to the C-module than Vβ (Figure 4D), similar to A6 (Chang-Gonzalez et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 4D and citation to previous study.

claim: Hα had greater amplitude in PC1 for B7low compared to B7high, suggesting a more pronounced asymmetric motion in B7low.
source: Amplitude of the hinge motion in the two chains varied, where Hα had greater amplitude in PC1 for B7low compared to B7high (Figure 4D, PC1 in bottom row). This suggests a more pronounced asymmetric motion in B7low.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 4D and involves inference about asymmetric motion.

claim: For B70, the small PC1 amplitude of the overall V-C motion without load does not suppress the motional asymmetry between α and β chains.
source: For B70, the small PC1 amplitude of the overall V-C motion without load (Figure 4C) does not suppress the motional asymmetry between α and β chains, while in B7high, the chassis becomes less mobile under load.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 4C and involves inference about motional asymmetry.

claim: ∠TCRα of B7low shows a wide bimodal distribution.
source: As in the case of low-load A6 (Chang-Gonzalez et al., 2024), ∠TCRα of B7low shows a wide bimodal distribution (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: ∠TCRα decreased at around 700 ns as B7low bent more, which would put the V-module in an unfavorable orientation to bind pMHC.
source: ∠TCRα decreased at around 700 ns as B7low bent more (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B). This would put the V-module in an unfavorable orientation to bind pMHC (Hwang et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and citation to previous work.

claim: The dependence of CDR3 distance on V-C angles was most steady in B7high.
source: The dependence of CDR3 distance on V-C angles was most steady in B7high (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The asymmetric V-C motion of the whole TCR controls the Vα-Vβ motion and the V-C orientation that in turn affects the stability of the TCR-pMHC interface.
source: This supports the allosteric mechanism by which the asymmetric V-C motion of the whole TCR controls the Vα-Vβ motion and the V-C orientation that in turn affects the stability of the TCR-pMHC interface.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation results about the allosteric mechanism.

claim: A typical heterodimeric protein-protein interface with BSA comparable to that of TCR-pMHC (∼1700 Å2) has sub-μM binding affinity.
source: A typical heterodimeric protein-protein interface with BSA comparable to that of TCR-pMHC (∼1700 Å2) has sub-μM binding affinity (Chen et al., 2013) while the affinity of the TCR-pMHC complex ranges between μM to hundreds of μM (Rudolph and Wilson, 2002; Rudolph et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The affinity of the TCR-pMHC complex ranges between μM to hundreds of μM.
source: A typical heterodimeric protein-protein interface with BSA comparable to that of TCR-pMHC (∼1700 Å2) has sub-μM binding affinity (Chen et al., 2013) while the affinity of the TCR-pMHC complex ranges between μM to hundreds of μM (Rudolph and Wilson, 2002; Rudolph et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Force generated during immune surveillance of αβ T-cells is utilized to discriminate cognate vs. non-cognate pMHCs.
source: Given the low equilibrium affinity, recent findings highlight the importance of mechanosensing, where force generated during immune surveillance of αβ T-cells is utilized to discriminate cognate vs. non-cognate pMHCs (reviewed in Zhu et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2021; Reinherz et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: The dynamical motion of the TCR chassis is responsible for the force-driven stabilization of the contacts with pMHC, i.e., catch bond formation.
source: Our earlier simulation studies of the JM22 and A6 TCRs showed that the dynamical motion of the TCR chassis is responsible for the force-driven stabilization of the contacts with pMHC, i.e., catch bond formation (Hwang et al., 2020; Chang-Gonzalez et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous simulation studies.

claim: TCRs do not have any structurally well-defined weak- or strong-binding states.
source: In contrast, TCRs do not have any structurally well-defined weak- or strong-binding states, which requires a different approach.
evidence: The claim is based on knowledge about TCR structural characteristics.

claim: Microsecond-long simulations of the complex under realistic pN-level loads and a combination of analysis methods are effective for elucidating the catch bond mechanism of TCRs.
source: As demonstrated in our present work as well as in our previous papers (Hwang et al., 2020; Chang-Gonzalez et al., 2024), our microsecond-long simulations of the complex under realistic pN-level loads and a combination of analysis methods are effective for elucidating the catch bond mechanism of TCRs, which shows that the load-dependent stabilization of the TCR-pMHC complex differs from simple relaxation of the structure in the initial crystallographic confinement.
evidence: The claim is supported by the current work and citations to previous studies.

claim: The load-dependent stabilization of the TCR-pMHC complex differs from simple relaxation of the structure in the initial crystallographic confinement.
source: As demonstrated in our present work as well as in our previous papers (Hwang et al., 2020; Chang-Gonzalez et al., 2024), our microsecond-long simulations of the complex under realistic pN-level loads and a combination of analysis methods are effective for elucidating the catch bond mechanism of TCRs, which shows that the load-dependent stabilization of the TCR-pMHC complex differs from simple relaxation of the structure in the initial crystallographic confinement.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation results.

claim: The mechanism of TCR catch bond formation does not conflict with assumptions based on steered MD simulation where partial unfolding of MHC and tilting of the TCR-pMHC interface were considered as required.
source: Recently, Choi et al., 2023, proposed a mathematical model of TCR catch bond formation. Their assumptions are based mainly on the steered MD simulation (Wu et al., 2019) where partial unfolding of MHC and tilting of the TCR-pMHC interface were considered as required. Our mechanism does not conflict with their assumptions since the complex in the fully folded state should first bear load in a ligand-dependent manner in order to allow any subsequent larger-scale changes.
evidence: The claim is based on inference comparing the current mechanism with previous models.

claim: Cα and Cβ domains form extensive contacts to construct a base, and the Vβ-Cβ contacts are more extensive than Vα-Cα contacts.
source: Cα and Cβ domains form extensive contacts to construct a base, and the Vβ-Cβ contacts are more extensive than Vα-Cα contacts.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data.

claim: The motional asymmetry affects the relative positioning of CDR loops, as measured by the CDR3 distance as well as the orientation of the TCR-pMHC interface relative to the loading direction.
source: In turn, the motional asymmetry affects the relative positioning of CDR loops, as measured by the CDR3 distance as well as the orientation of the TCR-pMHC interface relative to the loading direction.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation results.

claim: Unless an adequate load is applied to the complex to suppress the motion, destabilization of the interface occurs.
source: Unless an adequate load is applied to the complex to suppress the motion, destabilization of the interface occurs.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation results.

claim: The C domain renders a disadvantage to binding except under force.
source: As noted in A6 and JM22, the C domain renders a disadvantage to binding except under force.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation results and citations to previous studies.

claim: The increased interfacial stability of Vαβ-pMHC is consistent with the discovery that the C-module likely undergoes a partial unfolding to an extended state, where the bond lifetime increases.
source: The increased interfacial stability of Vαβ-pMHC is also consistent with our discovery that the C-module likely undergoes a partial unfolding to an extended state, where the bond lifetime increases (Das et al., 2015; Akitsu et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation results and citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: A logical evolutionary pressure would be for the constant domain to maximize discriminatory power by adding instability to the TCR chassis.
source: Therefore, while the variable domain dictates TCR fit with pMHC, a logical evolutionary pressure would be for the constant domain to maximize discriminatory power by adding instability to the TCR chassis.
evidence: The claim is based on speculation about evolutionary pressures.

claim: Single-chain versions of an antibody lacking the C-module (scFv) are in widespread use including CAR T cells.
source: Furthermore, considering single-chain versions of an antibody lacking the C-module (scFv) are in widespread use (Ahmad et al., 2012) including CAR T cells (Reinherz et al., 2023), a better understanding of a TCR lacking the C-module may help with developing a novel TCR-based immunotherapy.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The Cβ FG-loop deletion mutant of B7 TCR is predicted to possess a diminished catch-bond response.
source: Given the conservation of the asymmetric motion, we also predict the Cβ FG-loop deletion mutant of B7 TCR to possess a diminished catch-bond response, as our previous experiment (Das et al., 2015) and simulation Hwang et al., 2020; Chang-Gonzalez et al., 2024 demonstrated for other TCRs.
evidence: The claim is a prediction based on inference from previous experimental and simulation results.

claim: The crystal structures of A6 and B7 complexes have a comparable number of TCR-pMHC contacts, with a total of 33 for A6 and 29 for B7 in terms of residue pairs.
source: The crystal structures of the two complexes have a comparable number of TCR-pMHC contacts, with a total of 33 for A6 and 29 for B7 in terms of residue pairs, while the number of distinct atom pairs forming contacts are 46 for A6 (Garboczi et al., 1996a) and 63 for B7 (Ding et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: The number of distinct atom pairs forming contacts are 46 for A6 and 63 for B7.
source: The crystal structures of the two complexes have a comparable number of TCR-pMHC contacts, with a total of 33 for A6 and 29 for B7 in terms of residue pairs, while the number of distinct atom pairs forming contacts are 46 for A6 (Garboczi et al., 1996a) and 63 for B7 (Ding et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: During MD simulations, many of the contacts in crystal structures become transient, resulting in fewer high-occupancy contacts.
source: During MD simulations, many of these contacts become transient, resulting in fewer high-occupancy contacts.
evidence: The claim is based on observation from simulation results.

claim: In the thermally fluctuating state, there is a fourfold increase in the difference in number of contacts between A6 and B7 over the difference for static crystal structures.
source: In the thermally fluctuating state, there is a fourfold increase in the difference in number of contacts between A6 and B7 over the difference for static crystal structures (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of simulation data with crystal structures shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The Y5-D30α hydrogen bond in B7 is formed only in B7high, after about 300 ns.
source: In MD simulations of B7, the Y5-D30α hydrogen bond is formed only in B7high, after about 300 ns (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), and the Y5-Y101β nonpolar contact breaks during simulation of B70 and is not present in B7low (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B) while it persists with 62% occupancy in B7high and 52% occupancy in Vαβ-pMHC (Figure 2C and D; these occupancies are for the whole simulation period).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The Y5-Y101β nonpolar contact breaks during simulation of B70 and is not present in B7low while it persists with 62% occupancy in B7high and 52% occupancy in Vαβ-pMHC.
source: In MD simulations of B7, the Y5-D30α hydrogen bond is formed only in B7high, after about 300 ns (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), and the Y5-Y101β nonpolar contact breaks during simulation of B70 and is not present in B7low (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B) while it persists with 62% occupancy in B7high and 52% occupancy in Vαβ-pMHC (Figure 2C and D; these occupancies are for the whole simulation period).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figures 2—figure supplement 1A, B, C, and D.

claim: Changes to T-cell specificity by point mutations on Y5 are unlikely to arise solely from the size or the polarity of its binding pocket as a static structure.
source: Changes to T-cell specificity by point mutations on Y5 are thus unlikely to arise solely from the size or the polarity of its binding pocket as a static structure.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation results.

claim: Point mutations affect the organization and dynamics of the surrounding contacts in addition to fit.
source: Instead, point mutations affect the organization and dynamics of the surrounding contacts in addition to fit (Chang-Gonzalez et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim is based on inference and citation to a previous study.

claim: The inter-domain motion of TCR enables long-range allosteric discrimination of pMHCs, integrating the motion of the two entities such that they influence each other.
source: The inter-domain motion of TCR enables long-range allosteric discrimination of pMHCs, integrating the motion of the two entities such that they influence each other.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation results.

claim: The 14.5 pN force on B7high was applied under 190.0 Å extension, whereas the corresponding high-load simulation for A6 was with 18.2 pN at a slightly lower 187.7 Å extension.
source: The 14.5 pN force on B7high was applied under 190.0 Å extension (Table 1), whereas the corresponding high-load simulation for A6 was with 18.2 pN at a slightly lower 187.7 Å extension (Chang-Gonzalez et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Table 1 and citation to previous study.

claim: The average total intra-TCR contact occupancy for B7high between 500 and 1000 ns is 30.4±0.49 contacts, compared to 38.7±0.87 for A6 under high load.
source: The average total intra-TCR contact occupancy for B7high between 500 and 1000 ns is 30.4±0.49 contacts (Figure 1C), compared to 38.7±0.87 for A6 under high load (after 500 ns), which further supports a higher compliance of the former.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1C and comparison with A6.

claim: B7 will exhibit a weaker catch bond where the peak of the TCR-pMHC bond lifetime is at a lower force.
source: With its higher compliance, the B7 TCR-pMHC complex needs to be under a greater extension than A6 to apply comparable levels of force, and it would be more difficult to achieve load-induced stabilization of the TCR-pMHC interface. This leads us to predict that B7 will exhibit a weaker catch bond where the peak of the TCR-pMHC bond lifetime is at a lower force.
evidence: The claim is a prediction based on inference from simulation results.

claim: The destabilization of B7high at 1300 ns may have been a result of the constant-extension approach to apply load, which allows reaching low-force states by the compliant B7.
source: And the destabilization of B7high at 1300 ns (Figures 1D and 2B) may have been a result of our constant-extension approach to apply load, which allows reaching low-force states by the compliant B7.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from simulation results shown in Figures 1D and 2B.

claim: PA59 and PA25 TCRs share the same TRBV and TRBJ genes, and they share 11-aa CDR3β loops that differ only at a single position (Trp vs. Leu).
source: As a related example to A6 and B7 TCRs, PA59 and PA25 TCRs share the same TRBV and TRBJ genes, and they share 11-aa CDR3β loops that differ only at a single position (Trp vs. Leu) (Akitsu et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: PA59 and PA25 recognize the same pMHC (PA224-233/Db), and their maximum bond lifetimes and the peak catch bond forces differ considerably, 75 s at 21 pN for PA59, and 13 s at 15 pN for PA25.
source: Recognizing the same pMHC (PA224-233/Db), their maximum bond lifetimes and the peak catch bond forces differ considerably, 75 s at 21 pN for PA59, and 13 s at 15 pN for PA25 (Akitsu et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Differences in catch bond profiles may facilitate actions of the corresponding T-cells in tissues that present diverse mechanical environments.
source: These differences may facilitate actions of the corresponding T-cells in tissues that present diverse mechanical environments provided by cell movement, adhesion molecules, tight junction, and noncompliant inflammation.
evidence: The claim is based on speculation about the functional implications of catch bond differences.

claim: T-cells bearing A6 and B7 may perform differently in vivo depending on tissue localization even though they behave similarly in vitro in terms of cytotoxicity and secretion of select cytokines.
source: Likewise, T-cells bearing A6 and B7 may also perform differently in vivo depending on tissue localization (Akitsu et al., 2024) even though they behave similarly in vitro in terms of cytotoxicity and secretion of select cytokines (γ-IFN, MIP-1α, and TNFα) (Ding et al., 1998; Hausmann et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is based on speculation and citations to previous studies.

claim: The different catch bond profiles of A6 and B7 will render the two types of T cells to respond differently when the pMHC copy number on the APC is limited.
source: We also predict the different catch bond profiles of A6 and B7 will render the two types of T cells to respond differently when the pMHC copy number on the APC is limited (Akitsu et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim is a prediction based on inference and citation to previous work.

claim: Differences in the catch-bond profiles may affect the energy input for downstream signaling events that involve reversible conformational transitions in TCRαβ within a certain range of forces.
source: Differences in the catch-bond profiles may also affect the energy input for downstream signaling events that involve reversible conformational transitions in TCRαβ within a certain range of forces and extends the TCR-pMHC bond lifetime by more than an order of magnitude (Akitsu et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim is based on speculation and citation to previous work.

claim: Slight changes in interfacial contacts can result in altered distribution of loads across the TCR chassis so that changes in its dynamics affect interaction with CD3 signaling subunits.
source: Disparate biological outcomes between structurally similar TCRs recognizing the same pMHC are mechanically possible since slight changes in interfacial contacts can result in altered distribution of loads across the TCR chassis so that changes in its dynamics affect interaction with CD3 signaling subunits (Reinherz et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is based on inference and citation to previous work.

claim: The B7 TCR-pMHC model was built based on PDB 1BD2.
source: B7 TCRαβ-pMHC was built from PDB 1BD2 (Ding et al., 1998) using CHARMM (Brooks et al., 2009; Hwang et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim describes the methods used in the study.

claim: MODELLER was used to generate coordinates for missing loops in the Cα domain.
source: We used MODELLER (Sali and Blundell, 1993) to generate coordinates for missing loops in the Cα domain (S133-K136 and S170-D172 in the PDB numbering scheme) followed by a brief energy minimization.
evidence: The claim describes the methods used in the study.

claim: Distance restraints were applied to selected atom pairs forming contacts between the TCR and pMHC to prevent them from breaking during preparatory simulations.
source: To mitigate this, we introduced distance restraints to selected atom pairs forming contacts between the TCR and pMHC to prevent them from breaking during preparatory simulations.
evidence: The claim describes the methods used in the study.

claim: Production runs were performed using OpenMM with the CHARMM param36 all-atom force field.
source: Production runs were performed similar to Chang-Gonzalez et al., 2024. We used OpenMM (Eastman et al., 2017) with the CHARMM param36 all-atom force field (MacKerell et al., 2004) and the particle-mesh Ewald method to calculate long-range electrostatic interactions.
evidence: The claim describes the methods used in the study.
